name: Citizens Theatre
description: One of Scotland's flagship theatres, renowned for bold reimaginings of classic and contemporary work. Recently reopened after a major redevelopment.

name: Tron Theatre
description: A vital hub for new Scottish writing and independent theatre, housed in a converted church in the heart of the Merchant City.

name: Tramway
description: An internationally renowned arts venue in a former tram depot, presenting cutting-edge theatre, dance, and visual art.

name: Oran Mor
description: A converted hilltop church hosting A Play, A Pie and A Pint — Glasgow's beloved lunchtime theatre series.

name: The Glad Cafe
description: A community-focused cafe and arts venue championing grassroots music, comedy, and spoken word on the Southside.

name: Platform
description: Glasgow's dedicated venue for emerging artists and young people, with a strong programme of new work and community engagement.

name: Southside Fringe
description: An annual multi-venue festival celebrating the creativity and diversity of Glasgow's Southside communities.

name: Cottiers
description: A stunning converted church venue in Hyndland hosting theatre, comedy, music, and community events.

name: King's Theatre
description: A grand Edwardian theatre presenting touring musicals, comedy, drama, and the city's legendary annual pantomime.

name: Theatre Royal
description: Scotland's oldest theatre and home to Scottish Opera and Scottish Ballet, hosting world-class performances since 1867.

name: The Old Hairdressers
description: A DIY arts space in a former barber shop on Renfield Lane, hosting experimental performance, music, and artist-led events.

name: Mono
description: A vegan cafe-bar, record shop, and live venue on King Street with a packed programme of gigs, spoken word, and performance.
